spec.title: PROP-071: Change origin bindings and project-owned closure

p.NATIVE-ORIGIN-FIXTURE: A reusable feat declares native addressable facts and their explicit artifact requirements using PROP-043. Its intent is independent of a programming stack. A fixture binding selects an exact package coordinate/version together with exact fact addresses and captured authored manifest/document byte identities. The observed fact address and the versioned package selection are distinct; versionless fact metadata does not mean newest-slot authority. Leaf digests in this fixture establish byte identity, not original-package authentication.

p.ORIGIN-LOCAL-IDENTITY: Two consuming projects may reference the same immutable origin while authoring different local refinement and acceptance facts. Package fact addresses retain the package coordinate; local addresses retain their own project coordinate. A reference never copies package status into local authority. Consumer-owned materialization may add derived records but may not modify the authored package leaf bytes.

p.BINDING-OBSERVATION-FIXTURE: The initial change fixtures use the incumbent declared fact observation and requirements metadata query, retaining exact package/local addresses, authored artifact sets and separate authoring/adoption observations. Test-only fixture metadata does not commission a durable change parser, a closure evaluator or publication machinery. Fixture evidence may land before those later owners.

p.LOCAL-ACCEPTANCE-NOT-INHERITED: A package's authored done status, an absent or recorded adoption observation, and a copied status marker do not satisfy a selected local acceptance obligation. A copied paragraph, if valid local markup, is observed at its own local address; it does not replace a different selected local fact. Missing selected acceptance stays missing. Even a local done marker is not terminal proof by itself: PROP-043's declared artifact obligations and independent evidence remain separate. The metadata query reports no portable terminal verdict, and these fixture tests must not claim an acceptance runtime exists.

p.BINDING-PLANNING-INDEPENDENCE: Shared change intent and origin/local selections contain no personal owner/current/done scheduler state. Fixture personal-plan and work-coverage bytes are separate observations; editing them cannot rewrite shared binding, authored local obligations or immutable origin bytes. An adoption registry observation may change while shared intent stays unchanged. No second cursor or scheduler is created by observing these axes.

p.BINDING-TERMINAL-EVIDENCE-AXES: The incumbent terminal resolver receives the exact addressed fact's authored marker/requirements and an independently typed evidence-provider observation. Work coverage, adoption, authoring status and terminal artifacts are distinct. A work edge or personal done flag cannot replace missing or unavailable implementing evidence. Valid existing artifacts may be observed without fabricating a work item. Fixture checks use the existing terminal API and retain per-artifact states/locators, without promoting the requirements metadata report into a portable acceptance runtime. The initial fixture work observation is separate personal-plan data and an unattributed legacy refs bag; it defines no typed Work artifact or new registered relation.
